title: Rework BuildKit integration and add dependency-stability probes to CI
author: Ethan K. Park
description: Motivation: our monorepo build and release pipeline has been brittle due to a mix of legacy shell builders, inconsistent BuildKit usage across workflows, and no automated signal for transient dependency drift. This PR centralizes BuildKit integration into a single reusable composite action, introduces a lightweight builder image used in tests, and adds a CI job (dep-stability-probe) that detects lockfile/registry instability and surfaces it to release gating. Summary: 1) Add actions/ci-buildkit-composite: a composite action that wraps docker buildx setup, canonical cache-keying, and layer-level cache priming. 2) Replace ad-hoc bash builders in .github/workflows/* with the composite action. 3) Introduce docker/test-builder: small pinned image (FROM busybox + buildkit client) for faster containerized test setup used by unit/integration smoke jobs. 4) Add .github/workflows/dep-stability-probe.yml which uses a lightweight matrix to fetch package registries (npm/pip/crates), verify checksums against lockfiles, and record transient download failures to a short-lived artifact and Prometheus pushgateway for short-term alerting. 5) Update workflow cache keys to include repository-tooling-version and buildkit-pipeline-hash to reduce corrupt cache reuses. 6) Remove legacy scripts infra/scripts/build_and_push.sh in favor of the composite action and add migration notes in CONTRIBUTING.md. Checklist: - [x] Implement composite action and document inputs/outputs - [x] Migrate two long-running workflows (release-build, quick-ci) to new composite - [x] Add dep-stability-probe workflow and lightweight builder image - [x] Update tests to run with containerized harness - [x] Verify caches and rerun flaky jobs in CI - [x] Add release notes and rollout plan Context: this was driven by repeated CI incidents in Jan-Feb where build cache corruption and upstream registry timeouts caused spurious release failures (see SUP-4121). The dep-stability probe is intentionally conservative: failures are informational by default and only flip the release-stage gate when a threshold of transient failures is observed in 3 consecutive runs. Testing: local integration verified buildx cache priming reduces cold build time ~28% for the monorepo base image. The dep-stability probe was tested against intentionally-mocked registry timeouts; the job correctly marks an artifact and creates a short artifact bundle for debugging. Rollout plan: merge to main with feature flag OFF for release pipelines. After 48 hours of green CI, flip the release-gate flag in infra/ci-config.yaml to opt-in. Monitor the pushgateway metrics and pause if we see >5% increases in observed transient failures. Related work: this complements ENG-8342 (ci cache consistency) and reuses some of the cache-keying ideas from ENG-8427. Notes for reviewers: focus on the composite action inputs/outputs, cache key formulation, and the dep-probe thresholds. I also included small helper scripts under infra/ci for local reproductions; they should be treated as testing-only and are not intended for production automation.

review_comments: Asha Menon: Please split the composite action inputs; current single 'cache-key' string is hard to reason about. Also add more detailed docs for the priming step.

ci_checks_summary: dep-stability-probe: success (two registry transient failures recorded but below threshold)
release_notes: Centralize BuildKit usage via a reusable composite action, add dependency stability probe job to CI, replace legacy build script, and improve cache key hygiene. No breaking changes to public APIs. Deploy rollout guarded behind feature flag for release pipelines.
backout_instructions: If the composite action causes unexpected build regressions, revert the release-build workflow to the previous commit, and re-enable infra/scripts/build_and_push.sh from the release tag. To disable the dep-stability gate, set infra/ci/ci-config.yaml:release_gate.enabled = false and re-run release workflow.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: cache key churn could cause widespread cache misses on first rollout; Mitigation: staged rollout with opt-in flag and keep legacy cache key mapping for one week. Risk: dep-probe false positives; Mitigation: informational by default and require 3-run confirmation before gating releases.
